claims.text: Adding a controlled dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles to a refractory high-entropy alloy will enhance its mechanical performance.
Y2O3 addition will maintain the alloy's high-temperature phase stability.
Y2O3 addition will maintain the alloy's irradiation resistance.
A typical Nb-Mo-Ta-W refractory high-entropy alloy can have a single-phase disordered solid-solution structure.
Mechanical alloying followed by hot consolidation can create a uniform dispersion of 1–2 vol% nanoscale Y2O3 throughout the alloy.
The introduced Y2O3 nanoparticles will be distributed both within grains and at grain boundaries.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will impede dislocation motion.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will inhibit grain growth during high-temperature exposure.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will not coarsen under the stated high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will not alter the phase stability of the host refractory HEA under extreme conditions.
At approximately 800–1200 °C and about 1 dpa, the Y2O3-dispersed alloy will have roughly 10–15% higher yield strength than an identically processed oxide-free alloy.
At approximately 800–1200 °C and about 1 dpa, the Y2O3-dispersed alloy will have roughly 10–15% better creep resistance than an identically processed oxide-free alloy.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will retain phase stability similar to that of the oxide-free baseline.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will exhibit minimal irradiation-induced swelling.
The beneficial effect will persist at Y2O3 concentrations up to approximately 2 vol%.
Y2O3 concentrations significantly above 2 vol% may cause particle agglomeration.
Y2O3 concentrations significantly above 2 vol% may cause embrittlement.
Y2O3 concentrations significantly above 2 vol% may cause unexpected phase changes under high-temperature or irradiation exposure.
